pr_title: Split bsblan coordinator and randomize update interval
pr_body:
## Proposed change
Split the coordinator so we can catch the `BSBLANConnectionError` to avoid log spam with stack traces. Additionally, randomize the update interval to be less likely to hit a connection timeout when the device is already/still busy.

This may fix #97948 or at least reduce the timeouts and the log spam.

I ran this code on my production instance for a while and haven't had any new timeouts since.

It could be that HA is trying to update the climate entity while BSB-LAN is already polling the heater to send the data via MQTT. This often happens when BSB-LAN is polling some parameters, so the bus is blocked for other queries via HTTP.
Try disabling logging via MQTT in BSB-LAN so that HA is the only one polling the heater.

Thanks for the fast response. Disabling the MQTT logging is not my intention. I send more information via MQTT to display in HA. It is possible to increase the timeout limit of the BSBLAN integration?
If it is not possible I see (for me) the only way to increase the log level of the bsblan integration. I would like to use both :/

Yeah, sry if it was not that clear, that should not be the solution :) 

I just want to figure out if it is acutely BSBLAN or something network related.

Hmm, then it seems to be a network related problem. Is it connected via WiFi?
Yes, the bsb-lan adapter (WROOM) is connected via WiFi. The router is 2.5m far away (without any wall). The signal should be good/great.
Okay, I just see that I have the same error and mine is connected via Ethernet. I'm trying to figure out what is causing this.
Well, there was a problem reported in the upstream library: https://github.com/liudger/python-bsblan/issues/336
The timeout errors occur regularly (with and without MQTT logging). The issue was reported but I can not find a solution for the timeout.

For my part, I only get the timeout once when I restart HA because I use the `rest` integration to query additional parameters and both integrations block each other. Once both retried everything works fine.

@Gloomyeye maybe something from this thread (https://github.com/fredlcore/BSB-LAN/issues/586) helps?
Thanks for the hint. I will try the newest master version during this week.
The latest master version has no effect. Unfortunately, the error message still pops up regularly.

I did some testing and tried to reproduce it. As I wrote, I can reproduce it by polling BSB-Lan when it is already busy. I think the same thing is happening to you, even if you have disabled sending via MQTT, the parameters are probably still being queried in the background.

I may have created a bugfix that randomizes the update interval a bit to probably hit these timeouts less often. This also fixes the flooding of the log with stack trace in case of a timeout. In my case, I haven't had any new timeouts since then.
Thank you! As soon as it's released I'll test it.
